summary: Replica 40-foot fire lookout tower built in 2006 at the Oregon Department of Forestry's Tillamook Forest Center; climbable when the center is open.

facts.design: Replica fire lookout tower, 40 ft (12 m) tall, built for the visitor center

access.note: Open to the public to climb when the Tillamook Forest Center is open; admission is free, donations welcome.

visit.trail_note: A system of themed interpretive trails leads from the building, through the woods and along the river; a 250-foot suspension bridge over the Wilson River links to the Wilson River Trail.

events.note: Built in 2006 as a replica with education in mind (Roaming Civic); the 2006 Salem-News opening notice already describes the 40-foot replica
Tillamook Forest Center opened to the public on Saturday, April 1, 2006

notes_for_editor: The record's coordinates, county and replica status match the Forest Fire Lookout Association list, so no corrections. The Oregon Department of Forestry's own page returned only a browser-warning page, so ODF ownership rests on the Roaming Civic post and the Pioneer article. The Pioneer article's phrase that the tower was 'moved into place' was not used because it does not say where it was built. The replica has no original site; the story says so rather than inventing one. Facts use the center's 40-foot figure as the tower height. Web searches used: 1. Pages read: about 8, including one ODF page that failed.
